newsitem.title: USA: Simpson lawyer argues LAPD conspiracy, two killers.
newsitem.headline: Simpson lawyer argues LAPD conspiracy, two killers.

text.p: O.J. Simpson's ex-wife and her friend were killed by two people and police framed the former football star for the murders, a defence attorney in his civil trial argued on Monday.

Pointing to earlier high-profile cases that he said had embarrassed both the Los Angeles Police Department and the District Attorney's Office through their failure to get convictions, attorney Robert Baker told the jury, "They were going to win this one, they were going to get O.J. Simpson."

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994 murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman in 1995. He is currently battling a wrongful death lawsuit brought by the families of the victims, who are seeking substantial damages.

Winding up three days of defence closing arguments, Baker told the jury, "You can't give Fred Goldman his son back but you can give back Mr Simpson his life ... and give Justin and Sydney their dad back." Justin and Sydney are Simpson's young children from his marriage to Nicole Brown Simpson.
The jury was expected to get the case for deliberation either late on Monday or Tuesday morning following the completion of rebuttal arguments by plaintiffs' lawyers.
Baker said Simpson was the main suspect from the time the murders were discovered. "And if you don't believe that you might believe in the tooth fairy and the Easter bunny."

He described as "pretextual nonsense" the reasons given by detectives for going to Simpson's estate in the early hours of June 13, 1994: to notify him of his ex-wife's death and help him with the children, who were asleep when the murders were committed and were being looked after at a police station.
"If they were so damned interested in personal notification why is it that they didn't notify Fred Goldman until 5:30 that evening?" Baker demanded in a loud voice.
When police arrived, Simpson was in Chicago, where he had taken a late flight the previous night.

Baker, in his closing argument, said the main culprit in the conspiracy to frame Simpson was former detective Mark Fuhrman, whom he referred to as "the rogue Fuhrman." Fuhrman, who said he found a bloody glove on Simpson's estate the morning after the murders, was discredited at the criminal trial when defence lawyers showed he was lying when he said he had not used a particular racial epithet in the last 10 years.
Fuhrman subsequently pleaded no contest to a single charge of perjury and was fined and placed on probation. He did not testify in the civil trial.
"Fuhrman sees this glove (on Simpson's estate) and I suggest to you it's a glove he sees because he had planted it there earlier or at the same time that he allegedly found it," Baker said.
He named retired detectives Philip Vannatter and Tom Lange as Fuhrman's co-conspirators, saying they "lied" in testifying that Simpson was not a suspect when they went to his home.

Apart from a neighbour walking his dog near Nicole Brown Simpson's condominium, who heard a male voice saying, "Hey, hey, hey," at around the time of the murders, no one else heard anything, Baker said.

He argued that it took some time for Nicole Brown Simpson to be killed and that Goldman was present while the crime was being committed. "That to me says there must have been at least two assailants," Baker said.

Had there been only one, he argued, Goldman would have tried to prevent "this horrible, horrible" attack on Nicole Brown Simpson. Had this assailant been Simpson there would have been a "horrendous attack" on him by Goldman, Baker said. "But he had not one mark on his body," he said of his client.
